title: Summer Fruits Around the World
summary: Summer fruit can show us how people eat, shop, travel, and spend time together. Six countries offer very different examples, from tropical orchard visits to berry picking in a northern forest.

cover.alt: Four adults compare a table full of summer fruits in a courtyard with a market, tropical orchard, and pine forest beyond.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Summer fruit can show us how people eat, shop, travel, and spend time together. Six countries offer very different examples, from tropical orchard visits to berry picking in a northern forest.

items.prompt: Which fruit do you connect with summer?
Where do people buy fresh fruit near your home?
Do you prefer fruit that is sweet, sour, salty, or spicy?

blocks.title: Part 1: More Than a Cool Snack
paragraphs: On a hot day, cold and juicy fruit can feel very refreshing. However, summer fruits around the world do more than help people feel cool. They can also tell a story about weather, place, and daily life. A family may cut one large fruit and share it after dinner. A street seller may prepare a small fruit snack for one customer. In a tropical orchard, visitors can taste fruit near the trees where it grows. In a northern forest, people may carry baskets and look for wild berries. These are different activities, but fruit connects all of them. To understand a fruit culture, we can ask where the fruit grows, how people prepare it, and who eats it together.

images.alt: A learner watches fruit being picked from a tree, prepared at a cart, and shared by a family at a table.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: More Than a Cool Snack

items.prompt: What three questions can help us understand a fruit culture?
items.answer: We can ask where the fruit grows, how people prepare it, and who eats it together.
items.explanation: Which fruit would you choose on a hot day, and why?

blocks.title: Part 2: Spain — Two Fruits with Different Seasons
paragraphs: Watermelon and melon are important summer fruits in Spanish homes. Between June 2024 and May 2025, homes in Spain bought more than 660 million kilos of these two fruits. Their seasons are not exactly the same. Watermelon is most popular in the middle of summer, while people continue to buy melon into early autumn. This difference is useful when you shop: the best choice can change from one month to the next. Watermelon is often served cold and cut into large pieces. For example, a family can put a bowl of cold pieces on the table after lunch. At a picnic or the beach, one large watermelon is also easy for several people to share.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: Spain — Two Fruits with Different Seasons

items.prompt: How is the season for watermelon different from the season for melon in Spain?
items.answer: Watermelon is most popular in the middle of summer, but people continue to buy melon into early autumn.
items.explanation: Would you rather share cold watermelon at home, at a picnic, or at the beach?

blocks.title: Part 3: Thailand — A Visit to a Fruit Orchard
paragraphs: Thailand offers a very different summer fruit experience. In Rayong, orchard visits are especially interesting in June and July, when rain has made the land green and many fruits are ready. Visitors can ride through an orchard, stop near the trees, and then enjoy a fruit buffet. They may see soft-haired rambutan, purple mangosteen, large jackfruit, and heavy durian. Mangosteen has white pieces inside and a sweet-and-sour taste. Durian has a powerful smell, but its inside is soft, rich, and sweet. The buffet may also include mango with sticky rice and coconut milk. This example shows that fruit tourism is not only about eating. Visitors also see where the food grows and compare new smells, shapes, and textures.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: Thailand — A Visit to a Fruit Orchard

items.prompt: What can visitors do during a fruit orchard visit in Rayong?
items.answer: They can travel through the orchard, see fruit on the trees, and taste several fruits at a buffet.
items.explanation: Would you try a fruit with a strong smell if local people recommended it?

blocks.title: Part 4: India — One Fruit, Many Uses
paragraphs: India's hot season brings several special fruits. Litchi is a small, juicy fruit with a rough red skin, and it is harvested in summer in places such as East Champaran in Bihar. Mango also becomes the centre of public celebrations. At the Krishnagiri Mango Festival in Tamil Nadu, visitors can see different kinds of mango and foods such as pickles, juices, curries, and desserts. Jackfruit gives us another useful lesson. A ripe jackfruit has sweet yellow fruit inside, so people can eat it as a dessert or preserve it in syrup. A mature but unripe jackfruit can become chips, and tender jackfruit can be cooked as a vegetable. The same fruit can therefore move from a sweet snack to a savoury meal.

images.alt: A cook shows a learner an opened jackfruit beside ripe pods in syrup, jackfruit chips, and a savoury jackfruit dish.

blocks.title: Check: Part 4: India — One Fruit, Many Uses

items.prompt: How can ripe and unripe jackfruit be used differently?
items.answer: Ripe jackfruit can be eaten as a sweet fruit or dessert, while unripe jackfruit can become chips or a cooked vegetable.
items.explanation: Which would you like to try first: fresh litchi, a mango dish, or cooked jackfruit?

blocks.title: Part 5: Mexico — Four Flavours in One Snack
paragraphs: In Mexico, mango season runs mainly from April to August. Mango can be eaten fresh, but it also appears in juices, ice cream, sweets, fruit cups, and frozen snacks. One very concrete street-food example is mango prepared with chile, lime, and salt. The mango is sweet, the lime is sour, the salt is salty, and the chile is spicy. This means one simple snack can bring four flavours together. Chamoy, a tangy sauce that is often sweet, sour, salty, and spicy, is also used in mango snacks called mangonadas. Imagine a seller cutting a ripe mango into a cup, squeezing lime over it, and adding a little chile and salt. The preparation changes the fruit without hiding its fresh taste.

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: Mexico — Four Flavours in One Snack

items.prompt: What ingredients can people in Mexico add to fresh mango?
items.answer: They can add chile, lime, and salt, and some mango snacks also include chamoy.
items.explanation: Which of the four flavours would you add to fruit: sweet, sour, salty, or spicy?

blocks.title: Part 6: Türkiye — Fruit Connected to Place
paragraphs: In Türkiye, the names of summer fruits are often connected to farming regions. Malatya is known for apricots, Aydın for figs, and Kırkağaç in Manisa Province for melons. These names help shoppers connect a fruit with the place where it grows. In June, fresh apricots, figs, and melons begin to fill markets, while watermelon is another major summer favourite. Fresh apricots are soft and slightly sharp, but drying them makes their taste stronger and lets people keep them longer. Figs can also be eaten fresh or dried. Here is a simple family example: a plate of sliced melon, fresh figs, and apricots can sit in the middle of the table after a meal. Everyone can take a piece and continue talking.

blocks.title: Check: Part 6: Türkiye — Fruit Connected to Place

items.prompt: Which three places in Türkiye are connected to apricots, figs, and melons?
items.answer: Malatya is connected to apricots, Aydın to figs, and Kırkağaç in Manisa Province to melons.
items.explanation: Would you choose a fresh apricot, a fresh fig, or a slice of melon?

blocks.title: Part 7: Lithuania — A Basket from the Forest
paragraphs: Lithuania has a short warm season, so the arrival of berries can feel special. In Dzūkija, a forest region in the south of the country, looking for mushrooms and berries is a traditional activity. Wild blueberries are one of the foods that people can collect there. The experience is very different from buying fruit in a shop. A person carries a basket, walks slowly, looks carefully near the ground, and chooses only ripe berries. It also takes time and local knowledge. For example, a family might spend a quiet morning in the forest and bring a small basket home. They can eat the berries fresh, add them to pancakes or yogurt, or make jam for colder months. The fruit becomes both food and a memory of time outdoors.

images.alt: Two women pick wild blueberries into wicker baskets in a sunlit pine forest.

blocks.title: Check: Part 7: Lithuania — A Basket from the Forest

items.prompt: Why is berry picking in Dzūkija different from buying fruit in a shop?
items.answer: People walk through the forest, look carefully for ripe wild berries, and collect them in a basket.
items.explanation: Would you enjoy a quiet morning picking berries in a forest?

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: The examples show three useful ideas: place affects what grows, preparation changes flavour, and sharing fruit can create a social moment.

items.prompt: Which country's fruit culture would you like to experience, and why?
